# Rootmere

> Archival genealogical research in Central and Eastern Europe. We read handwritten
> parish registers, revision lists and land records in Latin, German (Kurrent), Hungarian,
> Polish and Church Slavonic, and turn one surname into a hardcover book about a family,
> with every statement cited to archive, file and folio. A trade name of Elite Product
> LLC, California, USA. Working since 2021. Contact: hello@rootmere.com

## What we do
- Archival scouting, $190 — which archives hold records for a family's place, what
  survives, for which years, and whether a full search is worth commissioning.
- One traced line with a printed book, $3,400.
- Two-line family archive, $5,900.
- Named gift certificate, for when research cannot be finished by a birthday.

## Where to read us
- Newsletter (free, roughly weekly): https://rootmere.substack.com — practical pieces on
  finding a family's village and reading old handwriting, written for people doing this
  for their own family rather than for professionals.

## Where we work
The territories of the former Habsburg, Prussian and Russian imperial administrations —
today Poland, Slovakia, Hungary, the Czech lands, Romania, Lithuania, Latvia, Austria and
their neighbours, including the Jewish communities recorded across all of them. Borders
moved, so one village's records are often split between two modern countries. Families
from outside this arc are welcome to ask.

## Pages
- [Record retrieval for professionals](https://rootmere.com/partners/): for immigration
  attorneys, citizenship-by-descent practices and heritage travel operators. Archival scouting
  $190, cited findings, white-label.
- [Questions people actually ask](https://rootmere.com/faq/): burnt parish registers,
  Kurrent handwriting, how far back a family can be traced, cost, what arrives at the end.
- [What your great-grandchildren will find](https://rootmere.com/article-legacy/): what
  actually survives of a modern life, and why the century closest to the present is the
  one most at risk.
- [Why your family's history matters](https://rootmere.com/article-why/): the argument
  for family history by analogy with national history.
- [A gift that was theirs before they were born](https://rootmere.com/article-gift/):
  family history as a gift, including for people never interested in genealogy.
- [The story your family tells](https://rootmere.com/article-myth/): the four myths
  families repeat when the documents are gone, and what an unchecked story costs.
- [What survives, and where](https://rootmere.com/archives/): field guide to parish
  registers and revision lists, and how to cite a finding.
- [A generation for free](https://rootmere.com/article-revisions/): reading a
  nineteenth-century revision list column by column.
- [But surely it all burned](https://rootmere.com/article-burned/): why "the records
  were destroyed" is usually a conclusion rather than a fact — the diocesan duplicate,
  the civil registry's second copy, and the microfilm are separate objects in separate
  places, and most searches stop after checking one.
- [Thirty years of nothing](https://rootmere.com/article-gap/): what to do when a
  register series simply stops.
- [A village in 1583](https://rootmere.com/article-1583/): finding a village in a
  sixteenth-century tax register.

## What we do not claim
We cannot guarantee a specific ancestor, a noble line or a particular depth: books burn
and archives lose whole decades. For a rural family in this region, documented research
realistically reaches the late 1700s, sometimes further. If the records for a place did
not survive at all, we say so and return the fee.
